To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
TAT‐mediation of protein delivery in neurons occurs through a lipid‐raft‐dependent endocytic process and is inhibited by cholesterol sequestering agents.
TAT‐mediation of protein delivery in neurons occurs via endocytosis and that the TAT‐BCL‐2ΔLOOP protein is neuroprotective in cell culture models.
the loop deletion B‐cl‐2 protein is transducible to neurons by the HIV‐1 transactivator protein (TAT), which protects neurons against cell killing.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of neuroprotective strategies using protein transduction domains, which are short peptide sequences derived from the HIV‐1 transactivator of transcription protein, TAT.
the development of novel neuroprotective therapies for the treatment of neurodegenerative diseases such as stroke and Alzheimer's disease.
the use of protein transduction domains for the delivery of anti‐apoptotic proteins to neurons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of TAT‐fusion proteins for the delivery of neuroprotective proteins is feasible.
the loop deletion BCL‐2 construct is transducible in neurons, and is neuroprotective in vitro.
the TAT‐Bc‐2Δloop protein transduction domain is an effective tool for the transduction of Bc‐2 proteins in neural cells and may provide a new therapeutic approach for neurodegenerative diseases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TAT‐mediation of the Bcl‐2 loop deletion protein (TAT‐Δloop) is a viable approach for neuroprotection and may be useful for treatment of neurodegenerative disease and brain trauma.

we show for the first time that a loop‐deleted Bcl‐2 can be successfully delivered into neural cells using TAT protein transduction domains, and that this construct protects neurons against cell killing by trophic factor deprivation and apoptosis‐inducing agents.
the TAT‐mediating protein delivery is a promising approach for protein‐based therapy in neurodegenerative diseases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the TAT‐BCL‐2 protein is a viable candidate for protein‐based therapy of neurodegenerative disorders.
the loop deletion of Bcl‐XL and Bcl‐2 can be fused to the TAT protein and transduce into cells.
the TAT‐BCL‐2Δloop protein is a viable candidate for neuroprotection and that the mechanism of protein transduction is through an endocytosis process that requires cholesterol and lipid rafts.
